citations.claim: first in_arena violation at shrunk step 33 - body 0 exceeds right boundary
body 0 gained extreme horizontal velocity after body-body collision
body 0 one step before violation still inside arena

counterfactual.change: Reduced bodies[1].vx from 27.70 to 5.0 (one field) - lowers post-collision velocity of body 0 so it remains inside arena for 33 steps; this tests that excessive impact speed is necessary for the in_arena breach.

explanation: Shrunk scenario has 2 circles and a thin vertical wall. Body 1 (m~4.9, vx~27.7) falls/bounces then collides with stationary body 0 near x=16 at step 26-27. The impulse transfers excessive horizontal velocity to body 0 (vx ~30.64 at step 27, speed ~30.6). With dt~0.017 and 17-18 substeps, per-substep travel (~0.03) is small but the boundary collision at x=20 fails to prevent escape: by step 33 body 0 centre reaches x~19.45, so centre+radius ~20.25 exceeds arena limit by 0.25 (>0.15 tolerance). Reducing the impactor speed removes the high post-collision velocity and removes the violation, confirming high-speed body-body momentum transfer plus missed/insufficient arena boundary response as cause.
vision_note: From steps 30 to 32 the blue and red circles hover just above the top of a thin vertical wall and drift steadily rightward toward the arena edge. At step 33 the red violating body reaches the right boundary and visibly protrudes outside the arena, clipped by the border, while the blue body remains inside.
